summary: Weekly scan for 2026-09-28. WebFetch worked for most official pages this run (unlike the modest-result expectation in the runbook), so verification and discovery both relied on first-party fetches rather than search snippets alone. Verification: reviewed all 45 rotation-batch items by fetching each provider's own page; 42 succeeded and are listed in checked_active (most confirm ongoing active operation with no shutdown signals; a few pages loaded but had no explicit status language, and are marked low confidence). 3 items (oracle-cloud, vultr-kubernetes, inmotion-hosting) returned HTTP 403 from their official domains and could not be verified this run, so they are omitted from checked_active. Two material, first-party-confirmed findings are reported as status_alerts for manual review: Heroku's Feb 2026 'sustaining engineering' shift (no new features, no new Enterprise contracts, self-serve unaffected) and a lower-confidence signal that Granite may now be generally available rather than in preview. One identity update is proposed: linode-kubernetes's canonical URL now 301-redirects to akamai.com. Separately, aws-app-runner's existing 'sunset' status in the catalog was independently corroborated against AWS's own apprunner-availability-change documentation page and needs no change. Discovery searches across the query families surfaced two new-candidate proposals: Docker Sandboxes (Docker's new cloud AI-agent sandbox product, confirmed first-party, medium confidence) and Zoho Catalyst Slate (a frontend hosting product, confirmed first-party but with unclear GA/preview status, low confidence). No hard deletions, pricing, or identity/status changes were applied automatically; all such items are left for human review as required.

new_candidates.name: Docker Sandboxes
new_candidates.summary: Docker Sandboxes is Docker's isolated MicroVM environment for running AI coding agents (Claude, Codex, Copilot and others) safely, usable locally or extended to Docker-managed cloud infrastructure via a single CLI.
new_candidates.best_for: Teams running AI coding agents that need secure, fast-booting sandboxed execution without managing their own isolation infrastructure, moving seamlessly from a laptop to the cloud.
new_candidates.change_note: New candidate: Docker Cloud Sandboxes, announced September 24, 2026 at WeAreDevelopers North America; confirmed on Docker's own product page and press release.

new_candidates.name: Catalyst Slate
new_candidates.summary: Catalyst Slate is Zoho's frontend hosting product for deploying modern JavaScript frameworks (React, Next.js, Vue, Angular, Nuxt) with Git-based deploys, free SSL, preview environments and a global CDN, integrated with the wider Zoho Catalyst backend platform.
new_candidates.best_for: Teams already using or considering Zoho Catalyst's backend services who want integrated frontend hosting without per-seat pricing.
new_candidates.change_note: New candidate found via 2026 Vercel-alternative research roundups and confirmed on Zoho's own product page; the page does not explicitly state GA vs. preview status, so confidence is low.

updates.rationale: linode.com/products/kubernetes/ now issues a 301 redirect to akamai.com/products/kubernetes, where the product is branded 'LKE: Managed Kubernetes Engine' under Akamai Cloud. The catalog's parent_slug (akamai-cloud) is already correct; only the canonical product URL appears to have moved. This is an identity field change, so per policy it will not be auto-applied and needs manual review.

status_alerts.rationale: Heroku's own blog post 'An Update on Heroku' (heroku.com/blog, Feb 6 2026, by SVP/GM Nitin Bhat) confirms Salesforce moved Heroku into a 'sustaining engineering' model: no new feature development and no new Enterprise Account contracts are offered going forward. Self-serve credit-card customers (existing and new) are explicitly unaffected in pricing, billing or day-to-day service, and core platform functionality (apps, pipelines, teams, add-ons) continues operating normally. This is a material, first-party-confirmed scope change worth recording even though the self-serve product line stays generally available; recommend human review of status/availability wording.

granite.so's current homepage shows live paid pricing tiers (Hobby/Advanced/Professional) with immediate self-serve signup and no beta/preview disclaimers, which suggests the product may have moved from preview to general availability since it was last verified as 'preview'. This is inferred from marketing copy rather than an explicit GA announcement, so confidence is low and a human reviewer should confirm before applying.
